name: Major cyber incidents
value: EU cold-storage attacks; blood banks hit
summary: Refrigeration-control attacks spread to at least 11 European countries and French blood bank cold storage
state: Attackers tampered with internet-exposed refrigeration controls at supermarkets in at least 11 European countries from 2 Nov. Germany, Romania and the UK reported cases on 3 Nov, and France reported cold-storage units hacked at three or more blood banks on 4 Nov, with no products damaged (Al Jazeera). No group has claimed it. No national-scale outage of power, health or finance systems had been reported as of 6 Nov.
for_you: Shoppers may see stores discard chilled food or limit stock. Businesses running internet-connected building or refrigeration controls are exposed; the NCSC publishes guidance on securing such devices.
rubric_hit: Watch: attacks disrupting large companies and a critical service (blood bank cold storage) in several countries; no national-scale attack

sources.title: Al Jazeera — EU urges action as Germany, Romania and UK report supermarket cyberattacks

why: Ransomware and state hacking now shut down hospitals, retailers, carmakers and airports for weeks.
drivers: Ransomware gangs, state actors, zero-days, supply-chain compromises.

rubric.alert: National-scale attack on critical infrastructure (power, health, finance), or a destructive state-attributed attack.
rubric.watch: Ransomware or attack disrupting a large company or critical service, or a mass-exploited zero-day.
rubric.normal: No major incidents disrupting critical services this week.
